# Proposition 7.5 full-floor numerical checks

Floating point experiments, not a certificate. 0 of 6 packings meet the majority-arrival target; 0 meet the literal small-waste hypothesis of Proposition 7.5. The intended nonvacuous replacement is measured arrival >=3L/4; it was not achieved. All comparisons use 2e-7 as in the imported audit; positive-drop eligibility uses its 2e-10 geometry epsilon. A ratio above 1 alone can be within tolerance; witnesses are retained. Zero/zero is displayed as 0, nonzero/zero as signed infinity. Lower bounds are reversed into lhs <= rhs; thus all ratio columns use that direction.

Construction adapted from the published staircase constructor, with full floor, specified rise, explicit second tilt, and no artificial ceiling-clearance horizontal shift at the tilt join. All vertex caps and SAT filters remain for staircase cases. C instead uses the explicitly specified sheared stacks: layer i shifts by -T*i/(n-1) along the square tangent, with n=1000, T1=0.8, T2=T1+n(alpha1-alpha2), base separation1.02, and w=max(Y-zeta X) over candidate vertices plus1e-6. Each constructed packing is independently validated before profiles or flow. All original audit checks 1-8 are rerun, including every boundary and aligned level. Tube cost uses the audit interior representatives (up to 1e-7 from limits), while drop and Delta use limits. P6 uses literal skip thresholds; the imported audit uses its documented 2e-7 threshold offset. P3 second ratio is a signed-zero denominator diagnostic; its lhs and PASS/FAIL matter.

OUTCOME: 0 majority-arrival packings; P8 exercised on 0 packings. The requested substantive P8 test remains UNEXERCISED. Passing empty-arrival inequalities is vacuous; this is not evidence for the last proof step. The empty A/B staircases have cumulative gap deaths: a path crosses the seam under its column's lowest tilted square and the top-to-ceiling gap. Their sum is about sin(alpha)+(1-cos(alpha))/2, independently of entry point. At alpha=0.07 this is 0.0711673472109 > delta=1/32, so increasing L alone cannot restore arrivals. Arrival requires sin(alpha)+(1-cos(alpha))/2 < delta (hence alpha about 0.03 or less here). This diagnoses the specified construction, not an impossibility theorem.

Budget: A/B stop at first successful L in their stated lists; both C attempts are retained regardless of result. B was cut to L=80 after an exploratory L=240 (about 200000 squares) was interrupted during the expensive full-polyline ordering audit; no completed comparisons or arrival values from that interrupted B run are used here. Earlier A exploratory trials were rerun in this final version. An additional full-floor L=50, R=1 diagnostic also had zero arrivals (all gap deaths); it was inspected before the final run but not put through the complete audit and is not a completed case row. The original unsheared C trials were replaced before execution by two sheared constructions. No broader tilt or length optimization was run. Total runtime 264.534048 seconds; failed comparisons 0.
